author: sonnet
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Added a two-sentence summary of how the system works today and the new design, plus a short terms section, before the diagram.
Replaced the one-line flow sketches with numbered flows that show the stop points for unknown email, rate limit, invalid token, rejected password and transaction failure.
Specified what reset_tokens stores and how the token is matched (hash the URL token, look up the row).
Made the transaction explicit: save password, mark link used, delete sessions together; emails queued after commit.
Stated that the response does not wait for the send, and that the rate limit is per account.
Replaced 'the usual retries' with the actual behaviour: 3 retries, then logged and dropped, user not told.
Added handling for an unavailable breached-password check (reject, link stays live) and two open questions for unknown facts.
Step 1: killing earlier live links now means marking them used (not deleting), so they still count toward the hourly limit; stated in Terms and Notes.
Step 1: added what happens when putting the reset job on the queue fails (log it, still generic message).
Step 2/3: stated that the form keeps the token in a hidden field and sends it back.
Step 3: spelled out the conditional update (unused, not expired), rollback and expired page when a second submit loses; moved marking used to the start of the transaction.
Step 3: added that a failed queue put for the 'password changed' email is logged and the password stays changed.
Terms: defined a session; Notes: said who gets the 'password changed' email and what it says, and merged the no-notification note into one line.
Merged the 'Email sending uses the existing worker' note into the undelivered-email note, so retry and drop behaviour is stated once.
Cut the separate 'password changed email says the password was changed' wording; kept only the recipient.
Opening summary now names the three flows; trimmed 'Terms' wording on reset_tokens and sessions slightly.
Kept the diagram, flows and failure paths unchanged; no behaviour altered.
holes: Q5: What is the Email queue (what technology, where does it live), and what does the API server put on it? (author: The existing email queue's technology and location are not known to me; the brief says only that the API adds a job and the worker sends it. The design needs nothing more than that. The job holds the recipient and the link.)

Q10: How is the new password stored (hashing), and what does 'breached-list check' call: a local list or an external service? What happens if that check is unavailable? (author: The brief does not say which hash algorithm login uses, so I only say to reuse the existing one. It also does not say whether the breached list is local or an external service. I decided that if the check is unavailable the password is rejected with 'try again later' and the link stays live, which is the simplest safe handling. Both facts are listed under Open questions.)
